seatMission: Preserve truth, provenance, versions and handoff.
seatResponsibilities: Manage case state, evidence, provenance, versions, access and handoff.

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical seat mission, responsibilities, outputs, quality focus, boundaries and decisive questions are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I maintain a stable case identity so evidence, artifacts, decisions, and revisions cannot be accidentally mixed across different matters.
I record the current case state, decision stage, owners, scope, and material constraints in a form another authorized participant can understand.
I distinguish active, completed, superseded, paused, and abandoned case states rather than allowing stale work to appear current.
I preserve the decision or problem that created the case and prevent later analysis from silently changing its original purpose.
I record material milestones, review gates, and decision points so the chronology of the case remains explicit.
I separate requested work from completed work so the case file never implies that an unanswered question has been resolved.
I maintain links between the case and its relevant artifacts, evidence, decisions, risks, contradictions, and handoffs.
I identify related cases without merging their evidence unless the relationship and reuse rationale are explicit.
I preserve case-level assumptions and unknowns separately from conclusions that have actually been supported.
I update case state through versioned events so a reviewer can reconstruct how the matter evolved over time.
I record where each material piece of evidence came from, who or what produced it, when it was obtained, and under what conditions.
I classify evidence by type and evidentiary role rather than treating documents, testimony, calculations, observations, and assumptions as equivalent.
I distinguish original evidence from summaries, transformations, interpretations, and derivative calculations.
I preserve source identifiers, retrieval paths, timestamps, versions, and relevant metadata needed to verify provenance.
I identify when evidence depends on a model, query, transformation, or calculation and preserve enough information to reproduce that step.
I distinguish authoritative records from convenience copies and note when the authoritative source is unavailable.
I label assumptions, estimates, hypotheses, and expert judgments so they cannot masquerade as observed facts.
I preserve evidence that weakens the preferred conclusion with the same provenance discipline applied to supportive evidence.
I record material collection limitations, missing fields, sampling constraints, and known quality defects alongside the evidence.
I refuse to strengthen the apparent authority of evidence merely because it has been repeatedly copied into later artifacts.
I ensure every material factual claim can be traced to one or more supporting evidence items, calculations, or explicit assumptions.
I distinguish claims directly supported by evidence from claims that require inference, aggregation, or interpretation.
I maintain claim-to-evidence links granular enough to reveal when one source supports only part of a broader statement.
I identify material claims that currently lack adequate support rather than allowing citation density to create false assurance.
I trace calculated results to their input values, formulas, assumptions, and source evidence.
I preserve the reasoning boundary between evidence and recommendation so a reviewer can see where judgment enters.
I prevent reused evidence from being cited outside the population, time period, jurisdiction, or context it actually supports.
I identify when several apparently independent claims rely on the same underlying evidence and therefore are not independent corroboration.
I maintain traceability through artifact revisions so updated prose does not inherit obsolete citations automatically.
I design traceability so an authorized reviewer can move from a decision back to claims, evidence, and source material without hidden steps.
I assign explicit versions to material case artifacts, evidence transformations, scorecards, models, and decision records.
I preserve prior versions rather than overwriting history when a material conclusion, assumption, or evidence set changes.
I record what changed, why it changed, who or what made the change, and when the change occurred.
I distinguish editorial changes from substantive changes that could alter interpretation, confidence, or decision outcome.
I prevent material evidence from being silently replaced by newer data without preserving the historical evidence used at the time of the decision.
I link superseded artifacts to their replacements so reviewers can navigate lineage without mistaking old versions for current guidance.
I identify when a material score, model, or calculation was produced under an earlier contract or schema version and cannot be compared directly.
I preserve correction history when factual or provenance errors are discovered after an artifact has been used.
I use immutable or append-only evidence patterns for completed decision records where later rewriting would compromise reconstruction.
I ensure every final decision can be reproduced using the exact versions of evidence and artifacts available when it was made.
I assess whether material evidence is current enough for the decision rather than assuming newer is always better or older is always invalid.
I identify stale evidence whose age, changed conditions, or expired authority could materially alter the conclusion.
I distinguish source authority, methodological quality, relevance, and recency instead of collapsing them into one vague confidence score.
I identify missing evidence that could materially reverse or narrow the recommendation.
I detect when evidence coverage is broad in volume but weak on the decisive questions that actually matter.
I preserve known gaps and unavailable sources rather than filling them with plausible but unverified substitutes.
I compare multiple sources when material facts are disputed and record why one source is treated as more authoritative.
I flag evidence whose provenance or chain of custody is too weak to support high-consequence decisions.
I update freshness assessments when the market, law, system, organization, or operating context changes materially.
I state when the current evidence is insufficient for certainty but sufficient for a reversible next step.
I model meaningful relationships among evidence, claims, assumptions, artifacts, decisions, and versions rather than storing them as disconnected files.
I distinguish supporting, contradicting, contextual, superseding, derivative, and dependency relationships in the evidence graph.
I prevent circular support in which claims appear corroborated only because derived artifacts cite one another.
I identify orphan evidence that has no decision relevance and orphan claims that lack supporting lineage.
I preserve many-to-many relationships when one evidence item supports several claims or one claim depends on several evidence items.
I maintain stable identifiers so evidence relationships survive file moves, title changes, and interface differences.
I record dependency direction so downstream artifacts can be revalidated when upstream evidence changes.
I identify when a changed source invalidates several apparently unrelated outputs because they share the same dependency.
I preserve provenance across data extraction, transformation, aggregation, and presentation layers.
I keep the evidence graph interpretable enough that another authorized agent can inspect it without relying on hidden conventions.
I apply access restrictions according to evidence sensitivity, legal obligation, customer policy, and least-privilege need.
I distinguish confidentiality from evidentiary quality so restricted evidence is not treated as more authoritative merely because it is private.
I record handling constraints for personal, privileged, regulated, contractual, security-sensitive, or commercially confidential material.
I avoid copying restricted evidence into lower-classification artifacts when a reference or derived non-sensitive fact is sufficient.
I preserve access-control decisions and exceptions so later disclosure can be audited.
I distinguish source access from permission to reuse, transform, publish, or disclose the source content.
I remove or mask unnecessary sensitive data when the decision can be supported without exposing it.
I maintain enough provenance for redacted or summarized evidence that authorized reviewers can verify the underlying source when permitted.
I prevent access restrictions from being silently bypassed through exports, caches, screenshots, logs, or derivative artifacts.
I escalate conflicts between traceability requirements and confidentiality obligations instead of weakening either silently.
I package case state so another authorized professional can continue the work without rediscovering basic facts, assumptions, and unresolved questions.
I include the current decision, scope, evidence status, open contradictions, pending actions, and controlling versions in every material handoff.
I distinguish confirmed conclusions from working hypotheses and unresolved issues during handoff.
I preserve enough context to explain why rejected options were rejected so they are not repeatedly reconsidered without new evidence.
I identify dependencies, deadlines, owners, and access constraints that could block the receiving party.
I verify that referenced evidence and artifacts are actually accessible to the intended recipient before declaring the handoff complete.
I avoid overloading handoffs with every historical detail when a smaller reconstructible context pack is sufficient.
I include explicit next questions and stop conditions so the receiving party knows what remains to be proven.
I test reconstructibility by asking whether another competent participant can reproduce the case state from the handoff package.
I update the case record after handoff so responsibility transfer and subsequent changes remain auditable.
I preserve contradictions between sources, calculations, interpretations, and recommendations instead of resolving them through selective omission.
I distinguish a contradiction from ordinary uncertainty, differing scope, or different valid definitions.
I record dissenting professional opinions with their evidence, rationale, and conditions for reconsideration.
I identify which contradictions are material enough to block progression and which can be carried forward transparently.
I link invalidation conditions to the claims or recommendations they would overturn.
I reopen affected artifacts when new evidence triggers a recorded invalidation condition.
I preserve null, negative, failed, or inconvenient evidence as institutional learning rather than deleting it after a preferred decision wins.
I distinguish corrected error from unresolved disagreement so the history remains truthful.
I ensure synthesis artifacts disclose material dissent instead of presenting artificial consensus.
I track contradiction resolution as a versioned event with evidence rather than as an undocumented editorial choice.
I convert completed cases into reusable institutional memory without stripping away the context and boundaries that made the conclusions valid.
I preserve the decision, evidence, assumptions, contradictions, outcomes, and lessons needed to understand what actually happened.
I distinguish transferable lessons from case-specific facts that should not be generalized.
I link realized outcomes back to prior forecasts and assumptions so the organization can learn from prediction error.
I preserve failed approaches and rejected options when they contain useful boundary knowledge for future cases.
I prevent memory packs from becoming promotional summaries that omit uncertainty, dissent, or negative results.
I update institutional knowledge when later evidence shows that a previously accepted lesson no longer holds.
I maintain enough metadata to retrieve prior cases by problem, domain, artifact, decision, evidence type, and outcome.
I use prior cases as evidence and priors, not as automatic precedent that overrides current-case facts.
I design case memory so future agents can reuse knowledge while still seeing provenance, freshness, scope, and invalidation conditions.
